blocks.text: Conventional vs Addressable Fire Alarm System in UAE

Choosing between a conventional and an addressable fire alarm system depends on your building's size, layout, use and Civil Defence requirements. We design, supply and install both types, with their fire alarm control panels, in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah.
Conventional Fire Alarm System

In a conventional fire alarm system, detectors and manual call points are wired in zones, such as a floor or a wing. When a device activates, the fire alarm control panel shows which zone is in alarm, but not which device triggered it. Conventional systems are simple, reliable and usually cost less to install, which suits smaller buildings, shops, small offices and warehouses with a limited number of zones.
Addressable Fire Alarm System

In an addressable fire alarm system, each detector and call point has its own address on a wired loop, so the control panel shows exactly which device is in alarm and where it is. Loop wiring with isolators keeps the system working if a cable is damaged, and the system is easier to expand and to integrate with other life safety systems. Addressable systems suit larger buildings such as towers, malls, hospitals, hotels and industrial sites.

items.q: What are the four types of fire alarm systems?
items.a: The four main types of fire alarm systems are conventional, addressable, analogue addressable and wireless. Conventional systems wire detectors in zones. Addressable systems give each device its own address on a loop. Analogue addressable systems send readings from each detector, such as smoke level, to the control panel, which decides when to raise the alarm. Wireless systems use radio signals instead of cable. Firestone designs, supplies and installs conventional and addressable fire alarm systems in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah.

items.a: The cost of installing a fire alarm system in the UAE depends on the building's size, the number of zones or devices, whether the system is conventional or addressable, the cabling, and Civil Defence approval requirements. Addressable systems usually cost more upfront than conventional ones. items.q: Is Hassantuk connection mandatory for fire alarm systems in Dubai?
items.a: Hassantuk connection is required for eligible buildings in Dubai. Hassantuk is Dubai Civil Defence's smart fire alarm monitoring system. items.a: Yes. Firestone assesses your existing panel and devices, then extends or upgrades the fire alarm system for renovated or expanded buildings. This includes compatibility checks, panel reprogramming and updated as-built documents at handover.

items.q: How often should my fire alarm be serviced?
items.a: Fire alarm systems should be inspected and tested on a regular schedule set by your maintenance contract and the authority's requirements, with visits commonly quarterly or yearly depending on the building. Each visit typically covers detector testing, control panel checks and battery tests. Firestone provides fire alarm maintenance contracts in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah.

items.q: Do you maintain the fire alarm systems you install?
items.a: Yes. Firestone provides fire alarm maintenance, planned servicing and 24/7 emergency repair for the systems it installs and for existing systems. Maintenance contracts are available in Dubai, Abu Dhabi and Sharjah.

items.q: What should I do if my fire alarm shows a fault or keeps giving false alarms?
items.a: If your fire alarm shows a fault or keeps giving false alarms, report it to a fire alarm technician and do not disconnect or bypass the system. Common causes are dirty or faulty detectors, low batteries, wiring faults and failed devices.
